metadata.note: The Detroit, Toledo and Ironton (the DT&I, 1905-1954 passenger years) and the companies that ran its lines before it: the Detroit Southern (1901-1905), the Detroit and Lima Northern (Lima Northern 1896-97, DL&N 1897-1901), the Ohio Southern (1881-1901) and the Iron Railroad (1849/51-1902). Each predecessor is its own company and colour (Rule 4); predecessor features share geometry with the DT&I features. Henry Ford's ownership (1920-1929) and Pennroad/PRR control (1929-1970) were stock control only and are NOT splits; the 1914 Railway -> Railroad rename is not a split. Drawn from research/branches/detroit_toledo_and_ironton_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-05), using each block's drawable span.

not_yet_sourced: Ends that are the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end ([OPEN]): Jackson - Ironton 1915-1932 (both ends; the post-1932 coach-on-freight ran an unknown time, ended before Sept 1951); Detroit Southern Detroit - Lima 1902-1903 and Lima - Springfield 1902-1904; Detroit & Lima Northern 1897-1899; Ohio Southern Springfield - Jackson 1884-1896; Iron Railroad Ironton - Pedro 1858-1880 and Pedro - Centre 1858-1875.
Single-year [ANCHOR] spans: Detroit Southern Springfield - Washington C.H. 1904; Ohio Southern Lima - Springfield 1896 and Jackson - Cornelia (Wellston branch) 1896.

Malinta cutoff opening: 1925 (web summaries) vs c.1930 (Fowler). The old route via Tecumseh is drawn to 1925 and the cutoff from 1930, leaving 1926-1929 with no Durban - Malinta line drawn. Do not close that gap without a source.
Delray - Flat Rock is left undrawn 1928-1930, when Fowler puts the Detroit terminal at Dearborn; whether any train still used Delray then is not established.
DT&I 1905 start years are operator dates (company formation), not a timetable dated 1905.
The DL&N's 1899 Columbus - Detroit trains: route south of Lima not established.
Headways and average speeds are estimates everywhere except Springfield - Jackson 1933-1954 (one round trip a day, 1942 and 1951).
Adrian - Sand Creek: whether the DT&I had its own track or ran over the Wabash is not established (drawn on the Wabash).
branches_deliberately_omitted: Toledo Branch (Dundee/Petersburg Jct - Toledo, Toledo-Detroit RR leased 1916): drawable NONE - no passenger year sourced; Feb 1952 Guide 'TOLEDO DISTRICT' is freight-only.
DT&I-era Wellston Branch (Jackson - Wellston - Cornelia): drawable NONE for the DT&I era; only the Ohio Southern 1896 anchor is drawn.
Iron Railroad Etna Branch (Pedro - Etna Furnace - Ellison, 2 mi): a single 1880 anchor year on a 2-mile branch - omitted as too small and too thin to draw.

Kingman Branch (Sedalia - Jeffersonville - Kingman): its only dated passenger years (1880, 1884) belong to the narrow-gauge Columbus, Washington & Cincinnati / Cincinnati, Columbus & Hocking Valley, not the DT&I or its named predecessors - a different company's layer.
Lisman - Centre stub in the DT&I era: no DT&I-era passenger date (the Iron Railroad's 1858-1875 service on it is drawn).
Springfield, Jackson & Pomeroy and Springfield Southern (1878-1881): no cleanly attributable passenger year.
Jackson - Ironton before 1915 (Detroit Southern/DT&I c.1902-1914) and Washington C.H. - Jackson under the Detroit Southern: no dated stop.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Not drawn because freight-only (Rule 1): Detroit - Springfield after 17 Sept 1932 (Feb 1952 Guide 'Operated for Freight Service only'; Scofield and Briar Hill, Mich. daggered); Jackson - Ironton after the post-1932 mixed service ended (Royersville daggered by Sept 1951); Tecumseh District and Toledo District (freight-only 1951); Dearborn District after c.1930; Springfield - Jackson after 8 May 1954; the Grand Trunk Western (1980-83) and Indiana & Ohio eras, which were freight only.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap: 18.5 mi, of which 16.7 mi on OSM track tagged old_railway_operator=DT&I and 1.7 mi of untagged terminal track at Delray. No straight-line leg. No separate documented mileage for this piece; Delray - Durban together trace 39.4 mi against Fowler-MI's 41.3 mi from Fort St Union Station. The Detroit end is drawn to Delray, where the DT&I's own line (OSM 'Flat Rock Subdivision') meets the Detroit terminal tracks. The passenger terminal moved repeatedly (Fowler-MI): Union Station (Fort St) to c.1907, Michigan Central stations to c.1918, Jefferson Ave to 1927, Dearborn 1927-1930/31 (separate feature), Union Station again from April 1931, West End to the end in 1932. None of the approaches from Delray over other companies' track into those downtown terminals is drawn, so the line stops about 3-4 mi short of Fort St Union Station.

segments.note: The Detroit approach of the DT&I main line, carrying the through Detroit - Lima - Springfield - Ironton trains (Nos. 1/2 and others; gas-electric cars on Nos. 1/2 Delray - Bainbridge from 25 Oct 1926, MRR-P2). The 1905 start is an OPERATOR date - the DT&I was formed in May 1905 from the foreclosed Detroit Southern and passenger service ran on without a break (Fowler dates the DT&I Springfield station 1897>1932) - not a timetable dated 1905. The 1927 end: Fowler-MI says the Jefferson Ave terminal was used 'to 1927' and that trains then ran from Dearborn Station via the new line to Flat Rock until 1930/31, so this piece is left undrawn for 1928-1930 (the Dearborn - Flat Rock feature carries those years). That gap is a deliberate narrowing of the research report's 1905-1932 drawable span, not a known suspension: whether any train still used Delray in 1928-1930 is not established. Headway and avg_speed_kmh are estimates and are NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap and OpenHistoricalMap: 74.3 mi. Pieces: Durban - Dundee 2.1 mi on an untagged OHM grade; Dundee - Tecumseh on the OHM-mapped 'Detroit, Toledo & Milwaukee Railroad' grade (the later NYC/Michigan Central line the DT&I ran over as trackage, Fowler-MI 'operated over NYC'); Tecumseh - Adrian on the OHM 'Detroit, Toledo and Ironton Railway' grade; Adrian - Sand Creek 7.1 mi ON THE WABASH (NS Detroit District) because no separate DT&I grade is mapped there - whether the DT&I had its own parallel track or used Wabash rails between Adrian and Sand Creek is not established; Sand Creek - Wauseon 16.8 mi on OSM DT&I-tagged abandoned grade; Wauseon - Napoleon 12.6 mi on untagged abandoned grade; Napoleon - Malinta 6.5 mi DT&I-tagged. Tecumseh - Malinta traces 56.6 mi against 55.4 mi in the Feb 14 1937 employee timetable (MRR-TEC). No straight-line leg. Durban is not in Nominatim; it is placed at the Diann junction (41.933, -83.636) where OSM's DT&I 'Flat Rock Subdivision' ends and the 'DT&I Subdivision' (the Malinta cutoff) begins, consistent with Fowler's Durban MP 41.3 from Detroit Union Station (traced Delray - Durban 39.4 mi, plus ~3-4 mi Delray - Fort St).

segments.note: The original Detroit & Lima Northern main line: Durban - Dundee, NYC trackage Dundee - Tecumseh Jct, then Adrian, Sand Creek, Denson, Wauseon, Napoleon to Malinta (later the 'Tecumseh Branch'). Through Detroit - Lima - Springfield - Ironton trains ran this way until the Malinta cutoff (block 6) took them. The 1905 start is an OPERATOR date - the DT&I was formed in May 1905 from the foreclosed Detroit Southern and passenger service ran on without a break (Fowler dates the DT&I Springfield station 1897>1932) - not a timetable dated 1905. The 1925 end is the EARLIER of two conflicting dates for the cutoff opening (web summaries: 'Malinta Cutoff in 1925'; Fowler: 'opened c.1930'), collapsed to the earlier so as not to assert service that may not have run. Whether any passenger train stayed on this route after the cutoff opened is not established. This deliberately leaves 1926-1929 with NO Detroit - Malinta line drawn at all (neither this route nor the cutoff, drawn from 1930); do not close that gap without a source. Feb 1952 Guide lists the 'TECUMSEH DISTRICT' (Malinta - Tecumseh) under 'Operated for Freight Service only'; the branch was abandoned in pieces from 1978. Headway and avg_speed_kmh are estimates and are NOT sourced.
